Match that EXACT pixel-art identity: adult cowboy brown brimmed hat, red neckerchief, blue shirt, leather saddle, rich chestnut horse with black mane/tail. Most important: MATCH THE REFERENCE'S HIGH THREE-QUARTER OBLIQUE camera elevation, visible top planes and saddle/back, chunky strong dark contour clusters, not a profile side-view sprite. Four columns by four rows, EXACTLY SIXTEEN separated mounted rider sprites. One rider on one horse per cell. Equal 320x320 conceptual cells and ample empty gutters on completely uniform pure magenta #ff00ff background. No checkerboard, no labels, no divider lines, no scenery. HARD pixel edges, no antialiasing, no smooth painting. Consistent 70-pixel-tall conceptual sprite detail across cells, enlarged with nearest pixel look. Preserve horse body proportions, saddle position and body anchor; don't stretch limbs or change lighting. Upper-left light. NO DUST in ANY CELL. NO SMOKE except brief gun effect. All feet must be readable and uncut. ROW 1: four subtle neutral IDLE poses, ALL FOUR HOOVES PLANTED, weight-bearing, relaxed reins, only small ear/tail/hand movement; no raised leg, no walking, no suspended dust. ROW 2: four sequential WALK phases, alternating correct leg pairs with small body rise and opposing motion, same rider stance. ROW 3: four LASSO phases wind-up, overhead loop, extended forward casting loop, recover; horse remains planted under rider. ROW 4: four SHOOT phases aim, single muzzle flash, recoil, recover; horse remains planted; aim pistol along the horse heading. Each sprite occupies its own complete isolated cell. Do not make a composition or groups. NO different costumes or horses.
Every cell faces SCREEN UPPER-RIGHT (northeast), walking diagonally AWAY from viewer exactly like the reference mount. We see the cowboy's BACK and horse's LEFT rear quarter plus visible saddle top. Horse head is up-right of its tail. Keep this oblique angle even in shooting and lasso; never rotate into a side profile or front view.

detail: Every cell faces SCREEN UPPER-LEFT (northwest), walking diagonally AWAY from viewer, the opposite oblique rear-quarter of the reference mount. We see the cowboy's BACK and horse's RIGHT rear quarter plus visible saddle top. Horse head is up-left of its tail. Keep this oblique angle even in shooting and lasso; never rotate into a side profile or front view.
